brewing.notes: A safe starting point for dark tea: rinse once, boiling water, or simmer it the traditional way.

description:
A compressed brick of sun-dried tea made at the Yanjin tea factory in Zhaotong, Yunnan, sold mainly to Tibet.

Treat it as you would any dark tea: rinse it, use boiling water, and buy from someone who can say who pressed it and when.
history: Little is documented about it beyond its recipe and its Tibetan market.
processing: The main stock, Jin Yu, is coarse old leaf boiled for 3 to 5 minutes and sun-dried; it makes up 55 to 60 percent, with 35 to 40 percent secondary material.
harvest_season: Often made from coarser, later leaf, as with most dark teas.
taste_profile: Clean aroma and a mild, even taste.
vintage_note: Dark teas are sold by production year and many improve with several years of dry storage.
